messages:
taylor: throwing this out there — proposal: a tiny JSON "onramp" at the edge for the browser SDK that translates into our internal protobuf/gRPC stream. makes frontends trivial, avoids grpc-web deps. main downsides: translation layer, how Console/telemetry and quotas map. thoughts? :thinking_face:
jess: ergonomics win for sure. biggest risks are losing per-model visibility in Console and tricky CORS/auth flows. we need to preserve enough metadata in headers so per-route/model dashboards still work.
omar: quota/billing note: edge must resolve client creds -> tenant id BEFORE aggregation. otherwise billing+ratelimit will be wrong. require tenant id header copied into the translated request.
sam: grpc-web option keeps typed streaming and exact token accounting, but adds complexity for frontend. if we do shim, we should add explicit header passthrough and a translation trace/span so tracing shows the extra hop.
taylor: header sketch (edge sets these when translating):
```
X-RW-ORIG-ROUTE: /v1/chat/completions
X-RW-MODEL: rw-llama-1
X-RW-CLIENT-TYPE: web-sdk
X-RW-TENANT-ID: tenant_12345
X-RW-TRANSLATION-SPAN: <trace-id>
```
sam: where do we count quota? at edge for speed or at runtime for accuracy? idea: optimistic count at edge and async reconcile from runtime with correction job. show mismatch alerts in Console if delta high.
omar: agree. reconciliation job should emit metrics: reconcile.quota_delta, reconcile.rate, and fire alert if tenant delta_rate > 0.5%. also record reconcile.reason codes.
jess: rollout plan: feature flag + canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%. SLOs: translation.p95 < 20ms, translate.error < 0.2%, quota_mismatch < 0.3%. if breach -> rollback to grpc-web path. require translation spans in traces.
deploy-bot: pipeline note — create canary in eng-platform and add metrics: translate.success, translate.latency_p95, model.latency_p95, quota_mismatch_rate. recommend 24h windows per step.
taylor: I'll write a short RFC with header mapping, telemetry events (translate.start/finish, reconcile.correction), reconciliation job outline, and canary steps. will @jess @omar for review. thanks! :sparkles:
